newsitem.title: GERMANY: DGB rejects Kohl call for little, no wage gains.
newsitem.headline: DGB rejects Kohl call for little, no wage gains.

text.p: A top leader of Germany's DGB white-collar workers' union rejected on Wednesday a call by German Chancellor Helmut Kohl for workers to give up real wage gains for a few years to help cut jobless rates.
DGB deputy leader Ursula Engelen-Kefer told German television in an interview that workers have not seen real wage gains in recent years due to rising taxes and associated costs.
In addition, she said worker benefits were under attack by Kohl and said unions had done their part in recent years by accepting moderate wage increases.

"I believe the government must drastically change its ways," Engelen-Kefer said. "The deterioration of wages and the social injustices must be stopped. One has to stop trying to politically destroy the workforce."
